scenario: [LGRA.2.9.6.4] closes the directive set, and the compiler refuses any other `%` sequence with DS_VALIDATE_INTERP_BAD_FORMAT. Pin: `%j` (Python's day of the year, which DS does not admit) is not a TIME_DIR of [LGRA.2.9.6.1]'s grammar, so `dsc.strlit.lgra_2_9_6_1_format` reads the spec as bad and `dsc.validate.luni_11_2_format` raises the code — on a Time slot, so the refusal is the directive's and not the kind check's.
rules_ds:
schema E scope logical:
    id: Int key
    t: Time mutable

rule r:
    E e
->
    log info "day {e.t:%j}"
